children.text: Traveling abroad, whether for study or work, requires holding the appropriate visa. While both visas allow you to live in a foreign country for a certain period, there are important differences between them that are essential to know.
Differences Between a Student and a Work Visa
Student and work visas differ in several important respects:
Purpose:
a student visa is issued solely for participation in educational programs, whereas a work visa is intended for employment purposes.
Duration:
student visas are typically issued for the length of the study program, while work visas can be either short-term or long-term.
Right to work:
working while on a student visa is often limited (e.g., 20 hours per week), while a work visa allows full-time employment.
Requirements:
a student visa requires an offer of admission from an educational institution, while a work visa requires a job offer issued by an employer.
What Is a Student Visa

A student visa is a special permit that allows a foreign student to enter, stay, and study in a foreign country. This visa is intended for people who wish to receive their education at accredited educational institutions in another country. Let's look at the significance of the student visa using the examples of the US and the United Kingdom.
US Student Visa (F-1)
For those wishing to study in the
US
, the most common visa is the F-1 student visa. This visa is intended for full-time study at accredited colleges, universities, conservatories, or other academic institutions.
Holders of the F-1 visa are permitted to:
Study
Work on campus during their first year (a maximum of 20 hours per week)
Gain practical experience (OPT) for a certain period after completing their studies
UK Student Visa

In the United Kingdom, the student visa is issued to students over 16 years old. To obtain this visa, a CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies) document issued by an accredited educational institution is required.
Holders of a UK student visa can:
Study at an accredited educational institution
Work up to 20 hours per week during term time and full-time during holidays
Extend their visa for further study or transition to a work visa under certain conditions
What Is a Work Visa

A work visa is issued to a person who wishes to be employed in a foreign country. This type of visa often requires employer sponsorship and depends on the specific requirements of the country in question.
Main characteristics of work visas:
Issued for a specific job and employer
Often requires proof of qualifications and experience
Is often a basis for obtaining permanent residency
Unlike a student visa, a work visa is more difficult to obtain, as it depends on the employer's willingness to extend a job offer and act as a sponsor, as well as on the country's immigration policy.

Ultimately, your goals will determine which visa is more suitable for you. If you want to pursue education, the student visa is the best choice, while if your main goal is career development and employment, then you should choose the work visa.
